summary: Iteration 13 — Apple/Play submission blockers verified. (A) DELETE /api/auth/account works end-to-end: 9/9 backend pytests PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_account_deletion_iter13.py (JUnit at /app/test_reports/pytest/iteration_13_account_deletion.xml). A throwaway user was seeded directly in Mongo with a valid session, an analyses doc + local .mp4 in /app/backend/uploads/videos/<uid>/, a videos.files GridFS entry (filename=analysis_id), a comment doc, and an upload_chunks doc; DELETE /api/auth/account with the Bearer token returned 200 {ok:true}; every collection is 0 for that user (users, user_sessions, analyses, analysis_comments, upload_chunks, videos.files) and the local dir is removed; the used token then returns 401 on GET /api/auth/me. No auth -> 401 and bogus token -> 401 both verified. (B) Push-removal regression is clean: POST /api/analyses/{id}/comments still returns 200 and lists back correctly on the coach's own analysis; PUT /api/users/push-token returns 405 (endpoint fully removed). No references to expo-notifications/expo-device/push.ts/savePushToken/_send_push_notification/expo_push_token in source or node_modules. (C) Broader regression green: /api/plans 200, /api/health 200, / serves HTML, chunked upload happy path (2 base64 chunks via Form -> /api/analyses/finalize -> 200 processing with upload_chunks doc removed). (D) FRONTEND: verified on preview URL at 390x844: (i) with seeded demo_token_active the Profile tab loads with no red-screen, 'Delete account' button visible below 'Log out', first tap changes text to 'Tap again to permanently delete account' with red warning 'This permanently removes your account, videos and analyses. This cannot be undone.'; seeded user preserved (only 1st tap performed). (ii) With a throwaway user+session inserted in Mongo, both taps performed: 2nd tap called DELETE /api/auth/account, cleared session_token from localStorage, and redirected to landing '/'; Mongo confirms 0 users + 0 sessions for the throwaway id. One data-integrity BUG surfaced during code review + reproduced live: delete_account queries analysis_comments by user_id but add_comment writes only author_id, so comments authored by a deleted user remain (see rca_of_issue).

critical.issue: Orphan comments remain after account deletion. add_comment (server.py:1177) writes only 'author_id' on analysis_comments docs, but delete_account filters by {'user_id': uid} — so comments authored by the deleted user are NOT removed. Live-reproduced: inserted a comment with author_id=<uid> (no user_id), called DELETE /auth/account -> 200, then re-queried analysis_comments by author_id -> still 1 remaining. This is a GDPR / Apple review compliance issue since the deletion PR explicitly promises comments are wiped. Fix: change to db.analysis_comments.delete_many({'author_id': uid}) or, safer, {'$or':[{'author_id':uid},{'user_id':uid}]}.

rca_of_issue: BUG — orphan comments after account deletion. Reproduction: (1) insert a throwaway user + valid session; (2) insert an analysis_comments doc with only 'author_id' set to the throwaway user_id (matching what server.py:1177 writes in add_comment); (3) call DELETE /api/auth/account with the throwaway's Bearer token — returns 200 {ok:true}; (4) query analysis_comments by author_id — 1 doc still remains. Root cause: server.py:1596 uses db.analysis_comments.delete_many({'user_id': uid}), but the insert at server.py:1177 only stores author_id (no user_id). Because the delete filter never matches, comments authored by the deleted user linger forever. Impact: violates the deletion promise made in the PR description AND the Apple App Store account-deletion policy, which requires *all* user-associated content to be removed. Mitigation: replace the filter with {'author_id': uid} (safest and semantically correct) or {'$or':[{'author_id': uid},{'user_id': uid}]} for extra safety. Estimated fix: 1 line change in server.py + re-run test_account_deletion_iter13.py.
